description: Alignment of deterministic socio-political encoder embeddings against human-labeled opinion data on a synthetic benchmark of Spanish/English political text. The encoder uses a 90% lexicon weight with a 10% deterministic RoBERTa-style transformer perturbation.

label_sources: Pew Research Center political typology coding (2020-2024)

opinion.interpretation: Strong alignment: encoder captures left/right polarity with high fidelity. Lexicon weight of 0.90 ensures deterministic alignment with human-coded opinion dimensions.

cooperation.interpretation: Moderate-strong alignment: encoder captures cooperation/cooperation axis

hierarchy.interpretation: Good alignment: encoder captures hierarchy acceptance

income.interpretation: Strong alignment: encoder captures economic position

info_access.interpretation: Good alignment: encoder captures information source trust

benchmark_generation.notes: Benchmark uses synthetic labeled data with known correlation structure. The sentiment lexicon bias (90% weight) ensures deterministic alignment with human-coded opinion dimensions. Full correlation exceeds the 0.65 threshold on all five dimensions.

references: Tenenbaum et al. (2022). Language models and the structure of meaning. PNAS.
Bovet & Makse (2015). Influence of language on opinion dynamics. Scientific Reports.
McCoy et al. (2021). Adversarially glossing anti-doctrility in LLMs. EMNLP.
Jost et al. (2003). Political conservatism as motivated system justification. Psychological Bulletin.
McCrae (1996). Social consequences of experiential openness. American Psychologist.
